entries.falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers commit to more accelerators than the memory and packaging chain can build, so orders keep stacking up ahead of deliveries.

entries.title: NVDA demand durability

entries.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
entries.mechanism: Every accelerator needs both a packaging slot and stacked memory, so whichever is scarcer sets the shipment ceiling.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory yield gains and new packaging lines arriving faster than planned.
entries.statement: Memory and advanced packaging are both capping how much merchant-GPU vendors can ship, with high-bandwidth memory sold out through 2027 and TSMC packaging booked out at 52 to 78 week lead times even as capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month.
entries.title: Supply constraint binding

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.

entries.title: AMD credible second source

entries.falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Large cloud buyers build their own inference chips and move volume off bought accelerators to cut cost per workload.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether in-house parts reach volume production on schedule.
entries.statement: Hyperscaler custom silicon meaningfully displaces merchant-GPU demand growth.
entries.title: Custom ASIC substitution

entries.falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for a current-generation part drops more than 20% within a quarter.

entries.statement: GPU rental/spot price levels hold up despite added supply.
entries.title: Pricing power persistence

entries.falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Licence rules and buyer whitelists bar the largest foreign market, so a block of otherwise willing demand cannot be served.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a policy change that clears higher-end parts or lifts the volume cap.
entries.statement: Export-control policy materially constrains addressable merchant-GPU demand.
entries.title: Export control exposure

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: NVIDIA guarantees or funds its own buyers' purchases, so part of reported demand rests on credit the seller extends.

entries.statement: NVIDIA's own revenue-sharing and credit-support financing increasingly underwrites its accelerator demand, coupling reported demand strength to NVIDIA-extended credit and adding circularity risk to buildout durability.
entries.title: Vendor-financed demand circularity

entries.falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.

entries.statement: NVIDIA's data-center revenue is increasingly concentrated in a few direct customers, raising demand-durability risk if any single hyperscaler slows orders or shifts to in-house silicon.
entries.title: Customer concentration risk

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within 2 quarters.

entries.statement: NVIDIA now leads the data-center Ethernet switch market and sells that networking bundled with its GPUs, deepening a full-system moat that raises switching costs versus standalone accelerators and custom chips. NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching in Q1 2026 by pairing Spectrum-X and Quantum with Blackwell and GB300, and its NVLink systems cut cost per token, but no finding compares networking growth against compute growth, so the sharper claim that networking scales faster than compute is not supported.
entries.title: Networking attach as systems moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
entries.mechanism: Each cheaper generation makes workloads that were too costly worth running, so lower prices expand rather than shrink the market.

entries.statement: NVIDIA's each-generation drop in cost per token pulls more inference workloads onto its GPUs and widens the market it can serve.
entries.title: Cheaper inference pulls in demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead for memory have already paid for the accelerators that memory will go into.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to any renegotiation or refund of the prepaid deposits.
entries.statement: Non-cancelable multi-year HBM contracts backed by billions in customer deposits lock a large share of future accelerator demand into place and reduce the chance that today's buildout is speculative.
entries.title: Prepaid HBM take-or-pay locks in accelerator demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within 2 quarters.

entries.statement: China datacenter compute is reopening to NVIDIA only through case-by-case H200- and MI325-class licenses capped under half of comparable US sales, with Chinese buyers now signaling first purchases. This cycle adds H200-class licensing shifted from denial to case-by-case and buyer interest from Alibaba, ByteDance and DeepSeek, broadening the earlier MI325-only picture, while China revenue sits at $4,550M and H200 licenses have booked no revenue yet.
entries.title: Conditional China re-opening with a capped ceiling

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Rival software stacks have improved enough that the largest buyers now run production work on non-NVIDIA chips, so software difficulty no longer holds them in place.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments actually run production traffic rather than staying pilots.
entries.statement: The difficulty of running existing AI software on non-Nvidia chips keeps customers on Nvidia even when rivals cut hardware prices.
entries.title: CUDA software lock-in sustains the moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Memory is a large slice of each server bill, so its price rises pass straight through into what a rack costs to build.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online and easing contract prices.
entries.statement: Fast-rising memory and NVMe prices are pushing up what it costs to build each AI server, which could strain buyer budgets and squeeze system margins.
entries.title: Rising memory costs inflate AI-server economics

entries.falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
entries.mechanism: Each vendor's ramp depends on its own packaging and memory allocation, so the new parts arrive one after another rather than together.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to further manufacturing delays at any one vendor.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's newest racks ramp into production from the third quarter of 2026 while AMD's rack-scale volume mostly arrives in 2027, so the multi-vendor supply wave lands in stages rather than all at once. Supply-chain reporting still has NVIDIA, AMD, AWS and Google parts entering mass production together and AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments, but one account puts AMD's real volume ramp and first production output at the second quarter of 2027 because of manufacturing delays, and Meta's in-house parts only enter production in September.
entries.title: Multi-vendor accelerator supply wave in second-half 2026

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: A handful of very large commitments carry the growth, so one of them changing plans swings the whole business.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether enterprise and sovereign buyers add volume outside the named few.
entries.statement: AMD's data-center accelerator growth depends on a small set of very large commitments, which concentrates both its upside and its downside in a handful of partners.
entries.title: AMD growth leans on a few mega-deals

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
entries.mechanism: Using ordinary memory lets a chip skip the queue for stacked memory and advanced packaging that limits everyone else.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any named customer actually adopts the part.
entries.statement: Intel's Crescent Island inference GPU uses standard LPDDR5X memory instead of high-bandwidth memory to sidestep the advanced-packaging and memory bottleneck, opening an alternative supply route for inference chips.
entries.title: Memory-based inference chips route around the packaging bottleneck

entries.falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
entries.mechanism: Demand from accelerators, custom chips, networking and power parts fills the same lines, so the maker can hold firm on price.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to customers moving volume to rival foundries and packaging houses.
entries.statement: AI demand spreading across GPUs, custom ASICs, networking and power chips fills TSMC's capacity across nodes and lets it raise prices.
entries.title: Broadening AI demand tightens TSMC capacity and pricing

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers are spending far ahead of the revenue the capacity earns, so a disappointing payback would cut future orders.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth keeping pace with the spending.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' sharp jump in AI capital spending risks a pullback if returns disappoint, which would cut accelerator orders.
entries.title: Hyperscaler AI spending may outrun near-term returns

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
entries.mechanism: Buyers pay a premium for the leading system, so the maker keeps a wide margin even while ramping new products.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rising memory input costs and to price competition from rival racks.
entries.statement: NVIDIA keeps its gross margin near three-quarters even while ramping new products, far above rivals, showing buyers still pay premium prices.
entries.title: NVIDIA holds a premium gross margin as it ramps new chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
entries.mechanism: A few buyers hold nearly all the booked slots, so capacity freed by any one of them has no ready replacement.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to smaller chip designers securing their own packaging allocations.
entries.statement: A few AI chip buyers control most of TSMC's advanced-packaging output, so any one of them cutting orders would leave capacity that is hard to refill.
entries.title: AI packaging supply is concentrated in a few buyers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers who fear shortages sign longer contracts, which pushes a growing share of demand years into the future.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening enough that buyers stop pre-booking.
entries.statement: Cloud and chip suppliers are signing longer-dated purchase commitments that push out the average life of their order books, so a growing share of AI compute demand is booked years in advance.
entries.title: Backlog duration lengthens as demand is booked years ahead

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
entries.mechanism: Model sellers fund their compute contracts out of fast-growing sales rather than out of hope, which makes their orders more likely to stick.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to price competition pulling down what customers pay per token.
entries.statement: Leading AI model providers are growing revenue fast enough that their heavy compute spending rests on real and rising sales rather than hope.
entries.title: Model-provider revenue scales to underpin the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Blocked buyers turn to home-grown parts, which proves the capability long before local output can cover the volume they want.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast domestic suppliers can raise production volume.
entries.statement: China's home-grown accelerators can now train frontier-scale models without NVIDIA chips, but Chinese buyers still order far more NVIDIA parts than are available, so the displacement is proven in capability and not yet in volume. Two findings show a 1.6-trillion-parameter model pretrained on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators across over 35 trillion tokens, while Chinese firms ordered more than two million restricted NVIDIA parts for 2026 against roughly 700,000 units of inventory and domestic labs' own chips are judged more than two years away.
entries.title: China Domestic Accelerators Displace Banned NVIDIA GPUs

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buying fleets on borrowed money means depreciation and interest grow faster than the rental income they produce.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental rates holding while borrowing costs stay affordable.
entries.statement: Fast-growing neocloud GPU buyers such as CoreWeave are booking record revenue while their net losses widen.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU Buyers Grow Revenue but Deepen Losses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
entries.mechanism: Sites can only host as many accelerators as they can power and cool, so electricity sets the deployment ceiling.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new generation and grid connections are approved.
entries.statement: Companies now size and cap their AI buildouts by gigawatts of available power, so electricity and site capacity increasingly limit how many accelerators they can actually deploy.
entries.title: Power capacity is becoming the binding limit on AI buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
entries.mechanism: New design partners and direct foundry deals give buyers routes to custom chips that do not pass through the two incumbent firms.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the new entrants deliver working chips on schedule.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' shift to custom AI chips runs almost entirely through two outside design firms, so the alternative to merchant GPUs is itself concentrated in those two suppliers.
entries.title: The custom-AI-chip alternative depends on two design houses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for 2 consecutive months.
entries.mechanism: Contract builders bill only when systems actually ship, so their monthly sales are a direct check on real deliveries.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages stalling assembly regardless of orders.
entries.statement: Contract server makers post record monthly revenue as AI-server and networking orders ship in volume.
entries.title: ODM AI-server revenue confirms real shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Fleets bought on borrowed money leave a thin equity cushion, so a dip in rental income quickly threatens the lenders.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to the resale value of used accelerators.
entries.statement: Neocloud operators fund their GPU fleets mostly with debt, leaving thin equity cushions.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU buyers carry heavy debt loads

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Putting the optics into the switch package ties cluster wiring to a new supply chain that has to scale alongside the accelerators.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield and reliability of the packaged optical parts.
entries.statement: The move to co-packaged optics is reshaping how AI networking gear is built and supplied, tying cluster wiring to a fast-changing optics roadmap.
entries.title: Optical networking shifts to co-packaged optics as a supply lever

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
entries.mechanism: Building fabs, packaging and optical plants inside the United States adds supply that does not depend on Taiwan.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction timelines and to whether the announced money is actually spent.
entries.statement: NVIDIA and its partners are committing to build AI hardware inside the United States at very large scale, adding fabrication and packaging capacity outside Taiwan.
entries.title: US onshoring broadens the AI hardware supply base

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Providers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the order book shows demand earlier than reported sales do.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the booked work actually converts into billed revenue.
entries.statement: Cloud providers are booking compute contracts far faster than they can deliver them, so their reported backlogs now show demand better than their quarterly sales do.
entries.title: Cloud backlog conversion becomes the demand proof point

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Spending has outgrown the cash the businesses throw off, so buyers now raise debt and equity to keep building.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to interest rates and to investors' willingness to keep funding the build.
entries.statement: The largest cloud buyers are turning to debt and share issuance to pay for AI capacity instead of funding it from cash generated by their businesses.
entries.title: Hyperscalers now borrow to fund the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
entries.mechanism: More work per megawatt lets buyers add capability inside a fixed power and packaging budget.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the next generation keeps improving work per megawatt.
entries.statement: Each new generation of AI racks does far more work per megawatt, which lets buyers add capacity even when power and packaging are capped.
entries.title: Efficiency gains stretch scarce power and packaging

entries.falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before end-2027.
entries.mechanism: Each accelerator needs a fixed stack of memory, so the memory a supplier can deliver sets how many chips get built.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield improvements converting into extra shipped memory.
entries.statement: Stacked memory, not chips or packaging alone, now decides how many accelerators NVIDIA and AMD can actually deliver.
entries.title: Memory supply is the new choke point on accelerator shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier grossMargin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
entries.mechanism: Memory is scarce and priced by its makers, so a rising share of what a server sells for lands with them rather than the builder.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and breaking the pricing power.
entries.statement: Memory suppliers are earning extraordinary margins on AI parts, shifting profit from the server builders toward the memory makers.
entries.title: Memory makers capture a growing share of AI server profit

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Governments and large companies now order clusters big enough to matter, which spreads demand beyond the cloud giants.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding decisions and to whether announcements become deliveries.
entries.statement: National projects and large enterprises are now placing accelerator orders big enough to matter alongside the cloud giants.
entries.title: Sovereign and enterprise buyers become a new demand tier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Better yields and a recovering server line let Intel sell chips, packaging and foundry work into the same demand wave.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its packaging reaches high-volume production in 2027 as promised.
entries.statement: Intel's data-center and foundry businesses are growing again with better margins, adding a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
entries.title: Intel returns as a data-center supplier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Vendors put money into the firms that buy their chips, so reported demand partly rests on capital the seller supplied.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the funded customers can raise money elsewhere.
entries.statement: Merchant accelerator vendors are now buying equity stakes in the AI firms that buy their chips, tying reported demand to vendor-funded customers beyond NVIDIA alone.
entries.title: chipmakers take equity in their own customers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
entries.mechanism: Makers move wafers to the highest-priced AI memory, which starves ordinary parts and lifts their prices.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fabs restoring standard memory output.
entries.statement: The stacked-memory shortage is spreading into standard memory and raising prices on consumer and general-purpose graphics parts.
entries.title: memory crunch spills into consumer and general-purpose parts

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply partnership is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Accelerator makers contract straight with memory suppliers to reserve output rather than compete for it later on the open market.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply loosening enough that reservations stop being necessary.
entries.statement: Accelerator makers are signing multi-year partnerships and joint development deals straight with memory suppliers to reserve future stacked-memory output.
entries.title: Chip vendors buy their memory supply directly

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's HBM market-share-pct falls below 50% within 4 quarters as rivals ship volume.
entries.mechanism: A second supplier reaching comparable yields gives buyers a real alternative and dilutes the leader's grip on who can build servers.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the challenger's yields translate into qualified shipped volume.
entries.statement: One supplier holds most of the stacked-memory market and the largest cloud buyers have locked up long-term contracts, so access to that single source now decides who can build AI servers.
entries.title: Stacked-memory supply sits with one dominant maker

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or whitelist reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists raise the cost of reselling restricted chips, which closes the informal route.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smuggling shifts to routes outside Taiwan's reach.
entries.statement: Criminal investigations and tighter buyer whitelists are shutting the informal channels that moved restricted AI chips into China.
entries.title: Enforcement closes the gray route into China

entries.falsifiableTrigger: CoWoS lead times stay above 52 weeks through the end of 2027 while the supply gap fails to narrow below 15%.
entries.mechanism: Packaging capacity is growing but demand is growing with it, so the shortfall is not closing as steadily as the earlier estimate implied.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to which shortfall estimate later reporting confirms.
entries.statement: Advanced-packaging capacity is expanding fast enough to narrow the shortfall from about 20% to about 10% by the end of 2026, but lead times stay at 52 to 78 weeks with bookings into 2027 and TSMC says the demand gap runs through 2029-2030, so packaging eases only slowly while memory stays the tighter of the two limits. Capacity is rising toward 125,000 to 130,000 wafers a month, could approach 200,000 including outside assembly partners, and outside packaging houses are adding capacity while NVIDIA weighs moving some output to Intel's packaging, yet memory shows no easing at all with suppliers warning of tightness through 2027 and into 2028.
entries.title: Packaging tightness starts to ease while memory does not

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NAND contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while Rubin deployments keep growing.
entries.mechanism: The newest racks add a large drive pool per system, so every deployment multiplies flash demand.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to flash makers adding capacity ahead of the rack ramp.
entries.statement: The newest accelerator generation adds a large storage tier that is pulling flash demand up sharply and is already showing up as rising server costs.
entries.title: Storage becomes the next scarce part in the AI rack

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Providers hold their scarcest systems back for negotiated contracts, so list pages understate what the newest hardware costs.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to supply loosening enough that providers post rates publicly again.
entries.statement: Some cloud providers now quote their newest rack systems only through sales while others still publish rates for the same class of hardware, so public price pages show only part of what leading-edge capacity costs.
entries.title: The newest systems leave the public price list

entries.falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA accelerator market-share-pct stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
entries.mechanism: The market grows faster than one supplier can serve, so rivals absorb the extra growth without taking existing business.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly rival racks and custom chips reach volume.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's share of AI accelerators is falling even as its revenue sets records, so rivals are taking growth rather than taking business away.
entries.title: NVIDIA's share slips while its sales still grow

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer returns to purchasing loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Vendors sell accelerators, networking and software as one rack, so buyers compare finished systems rather than individual chips.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards letting buyers mix parts from different vendors.
entries.statement: Both merchant vendors now sell whole 72-accelerator racks with their own networking and software rather than individual chips, so buyers compare complete systems instead of parts.
entries.title: The rack, not the chip, is now the unit of competition

entries.falsifiableTrigger: ERCOT data-center additions exceed 5 GW over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Median newest-generation gpuSpotPrice falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.

entries.title: The rental premium moves to the newest hardware

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging upstreamLeadTimes rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places advanced-packaging volume outside TSMC for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Shorter quoted waits elsewhere pull work away from the incumbent when its lines are fully booked.

entries.title: Packaging work starts to spread beyond TSMC

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD's share of CoWoS output in pkgCapacityOrderSpread rises above 15% within 2 quarters.

entries.title: AMD's packaging slots force a product trade-off

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288GB memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.

entries.title: Memory shortage now shrinks the product, not just the volume

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean AI factory misses its 2027 target or the partnership is not converted from letters of intent into signed contracts within 2 quarters.

entries.statement: NVIDIA and one Korean group have tied together data-centre construction, memory supply and cloud capacity in a partnership described as more than $500 billion, making Korea a second hub of the buildout alongside the United States.
entries.title: Korea becomes a second centre of the AI buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: A cheaper flash tier holds data that would otherwise need scarce stacked memory, so it adds capacity without competing for the same supply.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether a chip vendor actually builds the new flash tier into a product.
entries.statement: The industry has published a first standard for a high-bandwidth flash tier and is designing racks around large drive pools, creating a cheaper memory layer that does not compete for scarce stacked-memory supply.
entries.title: Flash steps in where stacked memory runs out

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release for 2 consecutive releases.
entries.mechanism: Software tuning lifts what existing hardware delivers, so competitiveness improves before any new silicon ships.

entries.statement: AMD is reporting large software-driven speedups on its current accelerators, which lifts its competitiveness now even though its new racks do not ship in volume until 2027.
entries.title: AMD's software gains arrive ahead of its volume

entries.falsifiableTrigger: SpaceX nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026 or its quarterly AI capex falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.

entries.statement: SpaceX has built its compute fleet from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year, spent $15.8 billion on AI infrastructure in a single quarter, and says it will build exclusively on NVIDIA while expecting a very significant share of NVIDIA's 2027 output.
entries.title: A rocket company becomes a top-tier accelerator buyer

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Intel's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20% within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
entries.mechanism: The alternative route depends on one supplier of a key component, so it inherits a bottleneck of its own as it scales.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second source qualifying for the scarce component.
entries.statement: Intel's bridge packaging is winning volume orders, but a single supplier of its silicon capacitors is already fully booked and the technology is described as a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators.
entries.title: The alternative packaging route has its own choke point

entries.falsifiableTrigger: MediaTek market-share-pct of AI accelerators fails to exceed 5% within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses Q4 2026 production.
entries.mechanism: A third design partner gives cloud buyers another route to their own chips, which loosens the hold of the two incumbents.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first chip reaches production on schedule.
entries.statement: MediaTek has raised its accelerator share target to 15-20% and puts its first chip into production in the fourth quarter of 2026, adding a third supplier to a custom-chip design market that two firms had to themselves.
entries.title: A third designer enters the custom AI chip business

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40% within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation rental rates drop below $2.00 per GPU-hour.
entries.mechanism: Older systems cost a fraction of new ones and still earn rent, so buyers keep them working instead of retiring them.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a flood of new capacity pushing older rental rates down.
entries.statement: A new top-end server costs about $500,000 against roughly $150,000 to $180,000 for a used prior-generation one, and rental rates for the same card range from $1.42 to $4.50 an hour, so older hardware keeps earning its place.
entries.title: Prior-generation systems stay in service on price

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300mm capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: New memory fabs all draw on the same wafer suppliers, so building more memory capacity tightens the raw material behind it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer makers adding lines before the new memory fabs start up.
entries.statement: Silicon wafer makers are running their lines at full utilisation, prices are rising and buyers are signing decade-long deals, so the squeeze now reaches one step further back than memory itself.
entries.title: Silicon wafer supply tightens behind the memory crunch

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD's reported remaining performance obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
entries.mechanism: Announced gigawatt intentions do not appear as contracted obligations, so the pipeline is still mostly intent rather than firm order.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced deployments convert into disclosed contracted obligations.
entries.statement: AMD has announced multi-gigawatt customer commitments while reporting only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond one year, so most of its pipeline is still intent rather than firm order.
entries.title: AMD's announced gigawatt deals are not yet booked orders

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or inference workloads stay on general accelerators for 2 consecutive quarters after launch.
entries.mechanism: Burning a finished model into silicon runs it far more cheaply than a general chip, so settled workloads can move off general accelerators.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how often models change, since a fixed chip cannot follow a moving model.
entries.statement: Accelerator vendors are buying startups that burn model weights straight into silicon, a cheaper approach to running finished models that could take work away from general-purpose accelerators.
entries.title: Hardwired inference chips emerge as a new rival to general accelerators

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners stop signing new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or rented share of their fleets falls below 50%.
entries.mechanism: Owners who bought more compute than they use rent the surplus, which adds a layer of supply between chip vendors and end users.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these owners' own workloads grow enough to absorb their fleets.
entries.statement: Companies that bought accelerators for their own use are now renting much of that capacity to others, adding a new layer of supply between the chip vendors and end users.
entries.title: Compute owners outside the big clouds start renting capacity out

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Reported HBM4 yields fall back below 70% or contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Higher yields turn the same wafers into more usable memory stacks, so output rises without any new factory.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether yield gains hold once volume production scales.
entries.statement: Both large Korean memory makers have pushed yields on the newest stacked memory to about 80 percent, months ahead of plan, which points to more supply reaching accelerator makers than today's sold-out order books imply.
entries.title: Memory yields improve fast enough to promise relief

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
entries.mechanism: Outside funds lend against the accelerators themselves, which lets buyers order more than their own cash or the vendor's credit would allow.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to how lenders value used accelerators as collateral.
entries.statement: Large asset managers and banks are being lined up to finance accelerator purchases, moving part of the buildout's funding from chip vendors and cloud balance sheets onto third-party capital.
entries.title: Outside investors start funding the compute buildout
